title: Meet the 20 first-place apps from RevenueCat’s Shipaton 2026
snippet: A cozy habit tracker, a smarter snippet library, and a rooster that wants you out of bed: this year’s Shipaton winners offer plenty of new apps to explore. RevenueCat’s annual app-building competition drew 3,985 project submissions in 2026, according to its winner announcement. Across the 20 first-place categories, developers tackled everyday frustrations, built inventive games, and found new ways to connect people. You can get a look at every first place winner below, and read RevenueCat’s full winner announcement for every more. more…
fullText:
A cozy habit tracker, a smarter snippet library, and a rooster that wants you out of bed: this year’s Shipaton winners offer plenty of new apps to explore.

RevenueCat’s annual app-building competition drew 3,985 project submissions in 2026, according to its winner announcement. Across the 20 first-place categories, developers tackled everyday frustrations, built inventive games, and found new ways to connect people.

You can get a look at every first place winner below, and read RevenueCat’s full winner announcement for every more. 

Mio turns everyday habits into a cozy game

1st place • Grand Prize Winner

Keeping a routine is easier when there’s something to look forward to. Mio pairs self-care and habit tracking with a pixel companion that grows as you make progress. Check off habits, earn coins, and unlock new companions and collectibles, with friends and groups adding a social reason to keep going.

Mio took Shipaton’s Grand Prize, with RevenueCat highlighting its revenue and growth in a crowded habit-tracking market.

App Store  |  Google Play

Boop makes every dog walk a collecting adventure

1st place • #BuildInPublic

That dog you met on your morning walk can become part of your collection. Boop identifies cats and dogs and turns their photos into stickers for a digital book, giving pet lovers a playful reason to pay attention to the animals around them.

Creator Taiwo Omisore’s “100 Boops” challenge took the app into the real world, where printed pet portraits and conversations with owners helped shape the product. That hands-on approach earned Boop first place in #BuildInPublic.

App Store  |  Devpost submission

Nitelore puts neon racing in your pocket

1st place • Best Game Award

If you have fond memories of futuristic arcade racers, Nitelore has a familiar appeal: hovering vehicles, neon tracks, and plenty of speed. Chase your own ghost in time trials, take on combat races, or compete online.

Free tracks offer a starting point, while paid unlocks and daily and weekly challenges give players more to explore. RevenueCat’s Best Game judges singled out the art direction, effects, and haptics.

App Store  |  Google Play

See as Me makes color blindness easier to understand

1st place • RevenueCat Peace Prize

Explaining how you see color can be surprisingly difficult. See as Me: Colorblind makes that conversation visual, using a split-screen camera to compare different types and degrees of color blindness. A shareable link lets someone else see the comparison without installing the app.

Developer Javier Jiménez drew on his own experience with protanopia. That personal perspective helped the app earn the RevenueCat Peace Prize.

App Store

Clucky gives your alarm clock a personality

1st place • RevenueCat Design Award

Clucky’s rooster is determined to get you out of bed. Turning off an alarm can require solving a problem, moving around, or finding an object, bringing a little friction to the temptation to snooze.

Its personality runs through the entire interface, including a time picker that uses the rooster’s scrolling eyes and yellow beak. That consistent character, animation, and attention to detail earned Clucky the RevenueCat Design Award.

App Store

Adversary adds a twist to the memory game

1st place • Catvertising Award

Adversary starts with a familiar challenge: flip cards and find matching pairs. The catch is a hidden Danger card with no matching partner. Reveal it, and an ad becomes part of the board you’re trying to remember.

That idea earned Niv Ben-porath’s game the Catvertising Award. Players can continue with ads after an initial ad-free period, or choose a permanent unlock that removes ads and adds difficulty options.

App Store

Bubble Games brings everyone’s phones together

1st place • Next Gen Award

Put a few phones on the table, and Bubble Games turns their screens into a shared game board. Objects move between devices as friends compete in minigames, including a virtual hot potato.

Built by four software engineering students at Université Laval, the Next Gen Award winner uses the phones people already have to create a shared activity. Its Shipaton submission includes ten minigames. The winner announcement links to the Android release on Google Play.

Google Play

GRIDLOCK gives tic-tac-toe room to grow

1st place • HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money)

GRIDLOCK takes a game everyone knows and adds up to four players, online rooms, and eleven special moves. The result offers more ways to disrupt an opponent’s plans than the familiar three-by-three board.

Its HAMM Award win recognizes how the business model fits the game: a shared Credits currency connects rewarded ads, optional packs, and a subscription, while core modes remain free. Players can choose the option that fits how often they play.

App Store

Just Add starts dinner with what you want to eat

1st place • Influencer Award – Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen

Just Add begins with a craving. Type what you feel like eating, describe it aloud, or take a photo, and the app suggests three meals built around it, adding protein, fiber, and healthy fats to round out the plate.

Shopping support, hands-free cooking, and remembered preferences help carry the idea through to dinner. The winner of Abbey’s Kitchen’s nutrition challenge also impressed judges with a dinner-host feature that accounts for other people’s preferences.

App Store

SnipStash keeps reusable content close at hand

1st place • Influencer Award – Productivity: Christopher Lawley

The reply you send every week, the PDF you keep hunting for, and the image you paste repeatedly can all live in SnipStash. It organizes reusable text, images, and files across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with a keyboard, Mac quick palette, hotkeys, and Shortcuts bringing them within reach.

Private iCloud sync connects the library across devices. Its speed and native interface helped it win Christopher Lawley’s productivity challenge.

App Store

Rehearse helps you practice the difficult conversation

1st place • Influencer Award – Career Coaching: Leadership Heather

Knowing what you want to say and saying it aloud are different things. Rehearse – Hard Conversations gives you an AI counterpart to practice with before a difficult workplace discussion.

Choose from 33 prepared scenarios or bring your own situation, then review feedback on clarity, empathy, assertiveness, and structure. A prep card helps you take the useful points into the real conversation. The app won Leadership Heather’s career-coaching challenge for its focused, straightforward approach.

App Store  |  Google Play

Game Magnet saves the game you spotted in a video

1st place • Influencer Award – Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming

You see a game in a short video, mean to look it up later, and forget its name. Game Magnet lets you share the clip to identify the games and save them to your backlog.

Processing happens in the background, with a notification when the result is ready. Shelves, ratings, and ranked lists help organize what comes next. The app won Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming’s challenge by making discovery and keeping track of games easier.

App Store

FeelGood offers movement that fits your day

1st place • Influencer Award – Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice

FeelGood: Movement Menu starts with a short check-in about your energy, available time, and how you want to feel. It then offers a small menu of movement, with an appetizer, main, and optional sides.

The options span yoga, Pilates, strength, walking, stretching, and breathing. Rest is part of the experience, too. Yusra Salam and Ameena Malik’s app won Simone Sharice’s yoga and fitness challenge, with judges praising its calm, inviting design.

App Store

BoatBrawl gets friends into the same battle

1st place • Ship Kotlin Everywhere

BoatBrawl brings arcade boat battles to a group of up to eight players. Steer, fire, and scramble through interactive arenas, with bots and shared-screen play offering more ways to join in.

Rehaan Cubes and Ashwin K M used Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform to bring the game across phones and computers, including iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and the web. Its smooth browser play helped it take JetBrains’ Ship Kotlin Everywhere award.

App Store  |  Google Play

Trazo gives golf videos a broadcast-style finish

1st place • Most Viral App

Trazo: Golf Ball Tracer adds a ball-flight line to your own golf videos. Select the ball twice to start, and the processing runs on the phone.

Julian Praest’s app won Most Viral App for the way its team introduced the product through organic content. Golf humor and practical advice set up the tracer reveal, making the finished video part of the pitch. For golfers, the appeal is simple: make the shot easier to follow when you share it.

App Store

Grandfolio helps collectors identify their next find

1st place • Best App for Galaxy

One Piece Card Game collectors know that similar-looking cards can be very different finds. Grandfolio helps identify artwork variants, manage duplicates, and track collection prices and progress.

The Best App for Galaxy winner impressed judges with layouts that adapt to folded, tabletop, and open-screen use. There’s an App Store release for Apple users, too, making this a relevant discovery even if your collection starts on an iPhone.

App Store  |  Google Play

Let’s Get Support focuses on the people giving support

1st place • Replit’s Idea to Income

Let’s Get Support by 3Dadz is designed for partners, parents, and friends affected by someone else’s addiction. Check-ins, journaling, boundary-setting tools, and local resources give those supporters a place to focus on their own needs.

Joshua Burgess and Aaryn B. built the app from community conversations in British Columbia, using Replit to turn the idea into a live product. It won Replit’s Idea to Income award. The announcement links to its Android release.

Google Play

PoquitoTalk helps everyday conversations cross languages

1st place • The Growth Loop Award

PoquitoTalk: Bocas del Toro turns English into local Spanish voice notes for WhatsApp and helps translate the replies. The recipient doesn’t need to install the app, keeping the conversation in a tool people already use.

Creator Dorien Van den Abbeele drew on years of life in Bocas del Toro. Its Growth Loop Award recognizes extensive growth experiments and an honest account of what the measurements could show. The announcement links to Google Play.

Google Play

Parky! puts useful park updates on your Lock Screen

1st place • Keep Them Coming Back Award

Parky! combines wait times, dining availability, and memories from Disney and Universal visits. Built by former Disney Cast Member Chase Van Derrick, it aims to offer useful help throughout a park day.

Dining alerts can become conversations on the Lock Screen, where you can ask about another time or restaurant. Alongside queue Live Activities and recap messages, those interactive notifications helped Parky! win the Keep Them Coming Back Award.

App Store

In Your Own Words makes room for a minute of practice

1st place • Funnel Vision Award

In Your Own Words offers short, real-world speaking scenarios and feedback on pace, hesitation, and filler words. Speech analysis takes place on the phone, giving users a way to practice the words before they need them.

Natasha Wilson’s app won the Funnel Vision Award for connecting a web quiz, a relevant practice deck, and a web purchase that unlocks access in the app. The introduction to the product begins before the download.

App Store

Winner • Conflict of Interest Award

Friendpire turns the idea of a board-game night with friends into a shared hex-tile world. Gather resources, build farms and docks, and grow an empire together. RevenueCat employee Erik MacInnis built the game to make it easier to stay connected with friends who rarely find time to play.

Friendpire won the separate Conflict of Interest Award, which was open to RevenueCat and sponsor employees and judged by Shipaton participants. It is included here as an optional sidebar and is not part of the 20 first-place count above.

title: Google rolling out software updates for these Nest Cam and Doorbell models
snippet: Alongside updates to several of its other smart home devices, Google is rolling out software updates to several Nest Cam and Doorbell models. more…
fullText:
Alongside updates to several of its other smart home devices, Google is rolling out software updates to several Nest Cam and Doorbell models.

As it continues support, Google is rolling out software updates to six of its older Nest Cam and Doorbell models. The list includes:

Nest Cam Indoor (1st gen)

Nest Cam Outdoor (1st gen)

Nest Hello / Nest Doorbell (wired, 1st gen)

Nest Cam IQ Indoor

Nest Cam IQ Outdoor

Google does note that these updates are only available if you have migrated older Nest devices to the Google Home app, a process that’s been widely available to all users and Nest devices for months, if not years.  

Also noteworthy here is that Google is referring to Nest Hello, its original doorbell camera, as “Nest Doorbell (wired, 1st gen).” 

	

What do these updates actually bring?

Google details a changelog including improvements to Wi-Fi reconnections, faster Night Vision switching, and a fix for the status light on Nest Cam IQ.

Improved Wi-Fi reconnection stability: Fixed issues that could cause cameras to crash or stall when reconnecting after brief Wi-Fi interruptions.

Faster night vision switching when turning on the camera: Fixed an issue on Nest Cam Indoor (1st gen) and Nest Cam Outdoor (1st gen) where turning the camera on in low light or switching to night vision in the Google Home app could take 15 to 20 seconds.

Synchronized audio and video on Nest Doorbell (wired, 1st gen): Fixed an issue that could cause audio and video to fall out of sync and trigger unexpected device restarts.

Accurate status light behavior on Nest Cam IQ: Fixed an issue on Nest Cam IQ Indoor and Nest Cam IQ Outdoor where the status light ring could pulse blue (indicating it was waiting for setup) when Wi-Fi was disconnected on an already set up camera.

These updates are rolling out now and will install automatically in the background.

title: AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into the App Store
snippet: Hundreds of AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into Apple’s App Store after passing app review. The same apps were also available in the Google Play Store. An investigation discovered more than 400 apps, apparently created by a single Chinese organization. The apps allow users to upload photos and then generate sexual and violent deepfakes which could be used to humiliate or threaten victims … more…
fullText:
Hundreds of AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into Apple’s App Store after passing app review. The same apps were also available in the Google Play Store.

An investigation discovered more than 400 apps, apparently created by a single Chinese organization. The apps allow users to upload photos and then generate sexual and violent deepfakes which could be used to humiliate or threaten victims …

A Wired investigation discovered a network of more than 400 connected domains and apps with hidden abusive functionality.

Apps like Viefur [ostentibly used to add clothing to pet photos] often claim to be everyday services—such as language tuition or AI workout coaches. When accessed under certain conditions, however, apps in the network stealthily load a web interface allowing the generation of explicit AI sexual images and videos using photos users upload. The apps include AI scenes such as “bedroom rape” and “threatening knife,” where a man holds a knife to a woman’s neck.

	

Wired says that the network is “hiding in plain sight,” thanks to thousands of video ads for them published on Facebook and Instagram. Some of the apps have been around for a year and have passed review by Apple, Google, and Meta despite each having clear policies prohibiting harmful deepfake content.

Bait-and-switch tactics were used to pass app review. The apps normally show benign content, but a server check can activate the hidden features. Downloading the app after tapping an ad for the deepfake functionality on Meta platforms appears to be one of the triggers. Dozens of pornography photo and video templates can then be downloaded, with credits purchased to generate deepfakes from user-uploaded photos.

Apple removed 19 apps after Wired shared details.

We review every app before it’s published, and these apps complied with our rules when we reviewed them. After approval, their developers changed the website the app pulls its content from, replacing what we approved with pornographic content, and promoted it through pornographic ads hosted on a third-party platform.

The company recently strengthened protections against this approach. Meta says it has taken action against more than 10,000 ad accounts linked to domains associated with these apps.

title: Apple stock drops nearly 3% after hours following Q4 2026 results
snippet: Apple shares fell as much as 4.43% in after-hours trading on Monday during the company’s fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, before recovering some of those losses later in the evening. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple shares fell as much as 4.43% in after-hours trading on Monday during the company’s fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, before recovering some of those losses later in the evening. Here are the details.

Apple today reported its fiscal Q4 2026 results, with a 12% increase in revenue, another 12% increase in net profit, and record revenue from its Services category, following its first sequential quarterly decline in 15 quarters.

The results also included a 17% increase in iPhone revenue and a 24% increase in Mac revenue, but an 8% decline in Wearables, Home, and Accessories revenue, which Apple attributed to “a difficult compare against the launch of the Watch SE 3 and the AirPods Pro 3 in the prior year,” and a 10% decline in iPad revenue, which Apple attributed to supply constraints and a similarly difficult comparison against last year’s A16-powered iPad launch.

During the conference call, Apple CEO John Ternus, CFO Kevan Parekh, and COO Sabih Khan fielded questions from analysts about rising memory costs, recent hardware price increases, and ongoing supply constraints, including those affecting the iPhone Duo.

	

The executives also offered a mixed outlook for the holiday quarter, with Apple expecting its highest quarterly revenue ever, but slower year-over-year growth, lower profit margins, and continued shortages of Mac and iPad models.

After ending the regular trading session down 1.83%, Apple shares initially climbed 0.5% to $340.00 following the earnings release. However, as the conference call progressed, the stock reversed course, falling to $323.33, or 4.43% below Monday’s closing price. Shares then recovered some of those losses, ending the after-hours session at $328.81, down 2.81%.

Of course, post-earnings after-hours trading doesn’t necessarily reflect how a stock will perform during the next day’s regular session, so it remains to be seen how investors will react when markets reopen on Tuesday after digesting tonight’s news.

fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Yesterday NASA announced the latest addition to its X-series of experimental aircraft that have included the Bell X-1 that first broke the sound barrier nearly 80 years ago, and the more recent X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator. The new X-70 Fractal is designed to be a “high-performance, highly adaptable research platform” that NASA can use as a testbed for the development and testing of next-generation aviation technologies.

The agency only released an AI-generated image of the X-70 shrouded in smoke and shadows, but confirmed several of the plane’s capabilities. It will be a crewed aircraft with a cruising speed of Mach .75 that can reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet and will provide an “operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles.” The X-70 will be able to carry up to 2,000 pounds of experimental equipment either inside or outside the aircraft, and will feature “advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight.”

“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics.”

snippet: Ahead of the new Apple TV 4K’s November 13 launch, Apple today released an updated build of tvOS 27.2 exclusively for the fourth-generation model. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Ahead of the new Apple TV 4K’s November 13 launch, Apple today released an updated build of tvOS 27.2 exclusively for the fourth-generation model. Here are the details.

New tvOS 27.2 build available for upcoming Apple TV 4K

Last week, Apple released tvOS 27.2, alongside iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2, and visionOS 27.2.

The update brought a handful of new features to Apple TV 4K users, including a new Shuffle option for screen savers, more control over which photos appear in screen savers, and support for American and British Sign Language in select movies and TV shows.

Today, Apple released a new build of tvOS 27.2 (24K154), specifically for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, which is currently available for preorder ahead of its November 13 launch. For reference, last week’s build version was 24K122, which means the new hardware is getting a different build of the same software update.

At the time of writing, Apple has yet to detail what, if anything, has changed in the new build. The release notes for tvOS 27.2 remain unchanged, and there are no separate release notes for this specific build.

Likewise, the previous build, 24K122, remains the latest version for existing Apple TV models.

The new Apple TV 4K launches on November 13, starting at $299. Among its biggest upgrades are support for Siri AI, built-in far-field microphones for hands-free voice commands, and a new surround sound feature that lets users pair four compatible HomePods as front and rear speakers.

It also comes with a fourth-generation Siri Remote that supports Precision Finding and can play a sound to help users locate it. The new Siri Remote is backward compatible with previous Apple TV 4K models and the Apple TV HD.

snippet: The company is said to be significantly dropping the amount it's spending on AI for its engineering teams.
fullText:
In Brief

Image Credits:STR/NurPhoto / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. It’s a big change for a company that has worked to integrate the technology into its engineering processes.

In October, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for its engineering teams, decreasing it from $300 to $200, the outlet reported. And more cuts are in the works, with some allowances falling to $100 a day, sources tell Bloomberg. Outside engineering, Apple is reportedly weighing a daily limit as low as $25 a day.

TechCrunch has reached out to Apple for comment.

Earlier this year, a tsunami of tokenmaxxing took hold, with companies pushing staff to use AI as much as possible in the name of vaguely defined efficiency gains. The frenzy was short-lived, however, as bills for said tokens came due, and companies decided that token rationing might be a more fiscally sensible approach.

Concerns persist about an apparent gap between what AI costs to build and run and the (often unclear) productivity gains the technology is suppose to generate.

title: Microsoft Teams Hack Report Shows Old-School Attacks Are Still a Thing
snippet: By impersonating help desk personnel, hackers were able to infiltrate corporate systems.
fullText:
Over the last year, the public has been trained to view the biggest new wave of emerging cyberthreats as AI-driven. In fact, frontier AI models accelerating the pace of cyberattacks — and even jumping ahead so far that the models have to be paused in the case of Anthropic’s Mythos — have driven the cybersecurity conversation recently.

But a recent report from Microsoft detailing how hackers used its Teams software to infiltrate corporate systems shows that human hackers are still using social engineering scams to fool other humans into doing their dirty work.

According to the report, “threat actors used Microsoft Teams messages and calls to impersonate IT or help desk personnel and socially engineer users into granting interactive remote access, primarily through Quick Assist.” Once they were granted access by unsuspecting workers, the hackers were able to set up software using Python, Bun or Java runtimes, open up networks and grant themselves authentication, giving them free rein over corporate systems.

			

More from CNET

In order to open the door to all that activity, however, a human had to grant access to the intruder. “Both incidents began with Teams phishing messages and calls that impersonated support personnel,” the report stated. “The social engineering persuaded a user to establish an attacker-controlled remote session, primarily by guiding the user to open Quick Assist and provide the connection code. This gave the attacker hands-on-keyboard access to the workstation.” Presumably, the employees who granted access thought the people on the help desks reaching out were just doing their jobs to keep their workplaces safe and operations running smoothly.

Microsoft suggests verifying external IDs

In an email to CNET, a representative for Microsoft said the company is introducing AI-powered phishing detection that it says “uses conversation context to identify phishing and social engineering in higher-risk messaging scenarios, particularly first-contact chats with external users.”

The change was listed as part of Microsoft’s roadmap for the software, which was revealed last month. Teams will also add ways to report suspicious guest invitations and blur QR codes sent by external senders, according to that roadmap.

However, a lot of the burden of making sure these hackers don’t get through falls to companies and their employees. “Users should exercise caution with external connection requests and messages, including verifying a sender’s identity and requests before acting on them,” Microsoft’s spokesperson said. “Administrators can also block external Teams users and specify which users in their organization are permitted to chat or meet with people outside the enterprise.”

Human-led attacks can harness AI, too

Yu Cai, associate director of the Institute of Computing and Cybersystems at Michigan Tech, said social engineering attacks are definitely still widespread. “AI may be changing the cybersecurity landscape, but it hasn’t replaced the human hacker. Human-led social engineering attacks remain a major cybersecurity threat, even as AI cyber attacks continue to get the bulk of today’s headlines,” he said.

But Cai said AI attacks and human-led attacks aren’t necessarily in separate buckets. AI can help make social engineering hacks more convincing by providing tools like voice cloning or deepfake videos.

In the case of the Microsoft Teams hacks, Cai said that what was most surprising was how simple the approach was to gain access. “This is a great reminder that sophisticated attacks don’t necessarily have to begin as sophisticated hacks,” he said. “This Microsoft incident wasn’t caused by any vulnerabilities in the Teams software, but by employees naturally placing trust in communications that come through the tools they use each and every day.”

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Omar Gallaga

He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

title: Apple now lets developers offer discounts when users move to cancel subscriptions
snippet: Apple today rolled out a new subscription retention tool for developers looking to reduce cancellations. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today rolled out a new subscription retention tool for developers looking to reduce cancellations. Here are the details.

Retention messages now available to developers

During WWDC earlier this year, Apple announced Retention Messaging, a new feature that lets developers display personalized messages and special offers to users as they attempt to cancel their subscriptions.

Now, as the company explained in a new post on its developer blog, the feature is available, allowing developers to configure messages that “appear in the cancellation flow and can include text, images, or a special offer.”

If this sounds familiar, that’s because this is not Apple’s first attempt to help developers reduce cancellations.

In 2024, Apple announced Win-Back Offers, which allowed developers to offer discounts to former subscribers in an effort to bring them back.

What’s different about the new Retention Messaging feature is that it allows developers to reach subscribers before they complete the cancellation process, rather than after they’ve already canceled their subscriptions or let them expire.

Here’s Apple on how developers can configure these messages:

In App Store Connect, you can configure retention messages for your auto-renewable subscriptions, including subscriber eligibility and the wait time between messages. With the Retention Messaging API, you can choose which message to show each subscriber based on their subscription details. API access is available by request.

Apple’s documentation notes that developers can create up to 10 retention messages per app, each associated with one or more subscriptions.

title: Moto Buds Ultra 27 and Watch Fit 27 help complete the company’s new premium ecosystem
snippet: The duo of Motorola accessories will see a North American release in the coming months, featuring Motorola Qira integration. more…
fullText:
The duo of Motorola accessories will see a North American release in the coming months, featuring Motorola Qira integration.

If you’re planning on upgrading to the extremely ultra-level Motorola Signature 27 flagship phone this year, I have good news for you: you’ll have plenty of time to save up for Motorola’s accompanying accessories after you buy the $1,600 phone. Motorola isn’t announcing a specific release date or price for either the Moto Buds Ultra 27 or Moto Watch Fit 27, but here’s what you can look forward to when they eventually come out.

Starting with the Moto Buds Ultra 27, which Motorola calls its “most feature-packed pair of earbuds yet.” These sport Bose-branded ANC and SoundDesign tuning, plus six high-SNR microphones with two dedicated Voice Pickup Units in what’s now become a conventional wireless earbud design with tips. Motorola says it created the microphones not just for great sound quality, but also for content creation, which means they’re clearly confident in the quality of these mics.

The buds deliver around 8 hours of continuous playback on a single charge, and the included case adds another 37 hours of use. They’ve also got built-in Motorola Qira support, plus AI Live Translate, head gestures, dual connection and audio share (so you can pair them with two devices, or pair two sets of buds with one device), plus a wear detection auto-pause feature.

	

They also sport IP57 protection, support Google’s Find Hub, and feature 11mm dynamic drivers for crisp audio. Moto Buds Ultra 27 will debut sometime in the near future in two colorways: Pantone Reflecting Pond (dark blue), and Pantone Temple Gray.

The Moto Watch Fit 27 is the antithesis of the recently launched Motorola Watch Ultra, focusing more on daily health than anything else. That means nearly two weeks of battery life on a single charge (instead of a day or two as Wear OS watches have), plus a Polar-powered health engine that’s designed to get your health metrics right the first time.

The square design features a rotating crown and a customizable physical button below the crown, IP68 and 5ATM protection, Bluetooth connection, built-in Motorola Qira support, all in an aluminum frame. A 1.85-inch gOLED display sports ultra-thin 2mm bezels and Gorilla Glass 3 on top. The display supports always-on visibility, and the built-in Qira assistant gives you hands-free command of the watch’s abilities.

As for health metrics, this one supports SPO2 monitoring, stress insights, heart rate powered by Polar, menstrual cycle tracking, auto activity detection, step and distance counter, over 100 tracked workouts, and dual-frequency GPS for accurate tracking. The Polar engine also supports holistic tracking, including sleep, calories, inactivity, and active workouts. Moto Watch Fit 27 launches sometime in the future in three colorways: Pantone Stratified Sea, Pantone Pigeon, and Pantone Ballerina.

title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
snippet: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.
fullText:
OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers. 

In a new essay, Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. He lays out five policy priorities, spanning worker protections and education to AI safety and data center development. 

The essay comes on the heels of a stunning Democratic victory in the midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of Congress amid widespread voter frustration over the cost of living. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure. 

Unsurprisingly, many of Lehane’s proposals would encourage wider AI adoption and support the infrastructure expansion companies like OpenAI need to grow. The original New Deal established protections for workers and placed constraints on corporate power. It’s less clear how Lehane’s vision would hold AI companies accountable for the economic disruption their technology could create. 

“Invoking a New Deal metaphor is to invoke state capacity to actually benefit the public,” Brennan said. “This is written by a private company that is trying to advocate for policies for its own benefit. It is ahistorical at best and harmful at worst.” 

While AI wasn’t a dominant issue in the midterms, opposition to data centers emerged as a major bipartisan concern in several races in the midterms. And Lehane may be right that AI will become a bigger part of the conversation over the next two years.

Affordability is already shaping up as a key issue for the 2028 election as Americans grapple with inflation, tariffs, and the rising cost of living. AI could become an increasingly large part of that conversation as voters stress about data centers hiking up electricity bills, AI replacing their jobs, and technology’s economic gains flowing only to a handful of wealthy companies.

Lehane acknowledges many of these concerns, but he offers few concrete proposals to prevent AI’s gains from becoming concentrated. Instead, he largely pitches AI as a path to greater prosperity for Americans willing to embrace it.

Take his proposals for the tax code. He suggests incentives for workers to learn AI skills, easier capital access for entrepreneurs, and new approaches to employee ownership and profit-sharing. Those are not the same as binding requirements that would ensure workers share in AI-generated wealth or that companies pay the costs of displacing workers.

“I was struck by how much of this policy is for a future…that is already predicated on mass AI adoption and AI benefiting society, which we have yet to see,” Brennan said. “All of it is predicated on benefiting from AI’s upside.”

Brennan said it would make more sense to see things like a revised corporate tax rate or tax incentives for hiring human beings rather than automating jobs, as well as ways to keep companies from amassing outsize market power.

Lehane’s emphasis on expanding AI’s economic opportunities, rather than limiting potential harms, extends to data centers. He notes concerns about data centers while emphasizing the construction jobs and local tax revenue they could generate. He then warns that politicians who support a data center moratorium could jeopardize America’s lead over China, going so far as to compare that stance to the 2002 vote to authorize the Iraq war.

Lehane also makes child safety and education central to his proposed agenda, stressing the importance of age-appropriate protections and safeguards around AI companions for minors. He also warns against keeping AI out of classrooms, arguing that doing so could lead to inequality between wealthy students and “children in rural communities.” But the argument takes for granted that AI improves learning, a claim that remains unproven and one critics say deserves more examination than more funding or individualized attention from human teachers.

Lehane also calls for enforceable AI safety standards, independent evaluations, public oversight, and the ability to restrict AI systems or use a kill switch to shut them down — though recent studies show that OpenAI and other AI labs haven’t published comprehensive plans for what they would do if a model escaped human control. 

Brennan called these stances “disingenuous,” pointing to OpenAI’s history of opposing legislation designed to impose such measures. In 2024, for example, OpenAI opposed California’s AI safety bill, SB 1047, which would have mandated catastrophic risk evaluations and shutdown capabilities. Last year, OpenAI also sought to limit state regulation, arguing that states could undermine American innovation. The company has more recently shifted some of those positions, backing several state safety laws and saying it would be open to independent evaluators embedded in the company.

Lehane also argues that people should maintain control over consequential decisions made using AI, rather than handing off judgment entirely to machines. But that raises the question of what human control really looks like in a society where humans are increasingly being required to use AI in education, work, healthcare, and government.

Throughout his essay, Lehane frames AI as a technology that could give Americans back their sense of agency and economic opportunity. But he ties average Americans’ “middle class” success to participation in an economy increasingly shaped by companies like OpenAI. Whether his policies will meaningfully redistribute power or subtly entrench it is less clear.

TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI for more specifics on Lehane’s proposals and the company’s stances, but it did not respond by the time of publication.

title: Google will fix Nest devices that didn’t adjust for Daylight Savings, breaking alarms and more
snippet: Google says it will roll out a fix for Nest devices that were impacted by problems with Daylight Savings adjustments due to changes in Canada. more…
fullText:
Google says it will roll out a fix for Nest devices that were impacted by problems with Daylight Savings adjustments due to changes in Canada.

A number of Nest Hub and Nest Thermostat users on Reddit noticed this week that their devices were showing the wrong time following the Daylight Savings time change. 

This isn’t just a display bug, with real impacts including late alarms, delayed or broken automations, and altered schedules, among other impacts. The problem is specific to certain parts of Canada, user reports show, as changes in the country left some provinces skipping Daylight Savings changes while others kept the status quo. Google previously issued guidance on how to handle these changes on Android phones.

On Nest devices, though, adjusting time zones isn’t quite as easy, so this was a bigger headache.

	

Google is working on a fix, though, the company confirmed to Android Authority. In a statement, Google says that it is aware of the problem and working to resolve it.

Google is aware of an issue affecting a small subset of devices in some provinces in Canada where daylight savings is no longer observed. We apologize for any inconvenience and are actively working on a fix.

Google also replied to some affected users to confirm a fix is coming but, as of November 4, the fix does not appear to be in place.

title: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
snippet: Zipline raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart.
fullText:
Zipline has raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.

Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.

On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.

The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software,  said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network. 

Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria. The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S. in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina. The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.

But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States. Zipline received its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries. It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including with Uber earlier this year.  

Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan. Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius. Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip. 

The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year. This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

title: Nothing teases screen-less product launching next month, ‘couldn’t have been an app’
snippet: Nothing has confirmed it will launch a new “AI-native” product in December, something that “couldn’t have been an app.” more…
fullText:
Nothing has confirmed it will launch a new “AI-native” product in December, something that “couldn’t have been an app.”

In a post on Twitter/X, Nothing CEO Carl Pei says that the company is launching a new product in December. This “AI-native” product will not have a display and, apparently, “couldn’t have been an app.”

Our first AI-native product ships next month. It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.

Exactly what that means is unclear.

“It couldn’t have been an app” is a pretty common line amongst dedicated AI products such as recorders, which could very well be what Nothing is working on. The screen-less design certainly limits a lot of other possibilities.

	

The rest of Pei’s post talks about how the AI industry is searching for its ideal product and the tools we’ve used over the years, and really seems to imply Nothing’s product will be an ambient recorder of some kind when discussing the “context gap.” The most telling bit reads:

Meanwhile, the context that matters most never reaches the model at all. Think about the last time someone said something worth keeping: an idea over coffee, a throwaway comment that unblocks your whole week. What did you do? “Hold on, let me write that down.” Out comes the phone, and by the time you look up, the moment has moved on without you. Or you don’t bother, and it’s gone by the end of the day.

Whatever this product is, it’s set to start shipping to customers in December.

title: watchOS 27.3 beta adds new Siri Recap and Live Rewind features for Apple Watch
snippet: Apple has released the first beta of watchOS 27.3 for developers, including two new Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4: Siri Recap and Live Rewind. Apple first announced these features at its special event in September, saying they would “arrive in beta later this year.” more…
fullText:
Apple has released the first beta of watchOS 27.3 for developers, including two new Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4: Siri Recap and Live Rewind.

Apple first announced these features at its special event in September, saying they would “arrive in beta later this year.”

Siri Recap and Live Rewind 

As a refresher, Siri Recap creates high-level summaries of conversations that you can review later. When the feature is enabled, Apple Intelligence will automatically generate a title and key points that you can review in the Siri app on iPhone.

Apple says:

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment. Your summaries auto-delete after 7 days if you choose not to save them.

You can turn on Siri Recap in the Watch app on iPhone. When you enable it, you can set a schedule based on time and/or location, or you can manually turn it on or off. You can also access it via Control Center on Apple Watch.

Live Rewind, meanwhile, helps you recall what was just said in a conversation. You can activate Live Rewind by double-pressing the Digital Crown, and then see a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of a conversation.

Live Rewind recalls what was just said in the last 15 seconds by showing a text snippet on your Apple Watch when you double-press the Digital Crown, so you can catch something you missed or are less familiar with. You can ask Siri about the content of the snippet or simply save it to the Siri app.

Apple emphasizes that these features are designed with privacy in mind. For example, Live Rewind plays an audible chime when you use it, even if your Apple Watch is on silent. Live Rewind and Siri Recap do not identify and attribute speakers.

Siri Recap’s summary is described as a “brief, high-level summary of conversations,” not a transcript. Apple says it will “exclude sensitive information like financial information or government-assigned identifiers.”

Live Rewind text snippets and Siri Recap summaries are end-to-end encrypted. Apple says the features “do not create or store audio recordings, and raw audio used for processing is completely inaccessible to the operating systems, apps, the user, or Apple.” The company uses the S11 chip’s Secure Exclave to power the features, a “dedicated hardware-isolated compartment that processes audio in complete isolation from the rest of the system, then immediately deletes it.”

Apple has published a detailed Privacy Overview covering the Audio Intelligence features on its website, as well as a support article:

Audio Intelligence Privacy Overview

Audio Intelligence Support Article

Siri Recap and Live Rewind are available in beta with watchOS 27.3, which is available now for developers.

title: How North Korean Hackers Stole $6 Billion in Crypto From Binance
snippet: A fake job interview scam helped hackers get their hands into Binance’s systems.
fullText:
The popular cryptocurrency exchange Binance was hit by hackers on Oct. 29. The company confirmed that attackers gained access to its servers and stole $6.3 billion, with analysts calling it one of the biggest thefts in cryptocurrency history.

While investigating the breach, the FBI confirmed that a known group of North Korean hackers who use the name “TradeTraitor” was behind the hack. Binance initially said hackers likely used an employee’s laptop to gain access to their servers. Now, the company added that hackers likely gained access to its systems in June, and then, using a recruitment scam that involved fake job interviews in September, gained a further foothold that let them steal billions in October.

The company temporarily paused all withdrawals at the end of October and resumed them on Nov. 1.

			

More from CNET

Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private… pic.twitter.com/5REncAI77y

— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026

The company says it “will cover all losses” for affected traders using its secured reserves and funds. As of Nov. 4, the company has “now replenished approximately 98% of the impacted amount,” it said in an X post. The last bit is expected to take longer to acquire. That’s because of the $6.34 billion in losses. Binance is holding $5 billion in exact token assets, with plans to purchase the rest through other market channels.

“We are doing this to match the format of the remaining token assets and address any asset shortfalls,” a Binance spokesperson told CNET on Oct. 30. So if you lost money in the form of bitcoin, you would ideally be reimbursed in bitcoin, not another cryptocurrency. 

Crypto prices fell across the board upon the news of the Binance breach. Cryptocurrency isn’t regulated like other stock markets or banks. Crypto markets are constantly open, and traders “mine” currency using complex computations that use a lot of energy. (If that sounds familiar, it’s because a lot of crypto operations were the blueprint for AI data centers.) Binance is not insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the government agency that protects your bank deposits (up to a certain amount) if your bank fails.

Cybersecurity breaches are increasingly escalating, thanks to AI powering both defenders and attackers. Polymarket, another crypto trading platform, temporarily paused trading on Oct. 29 due to a third-party vendor issue, which was also referred to law enforcement, according to the company. But the Binance hack may be the “largest hack in history,” according to blockchain research firm TRM.

title: Apple Photos keeps getting better, here’s what’s new in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27’s biggest highlight is Siri AI, but the update also packs new features for apps like Messages, Notes, Wallet, and more. Here’s everything new for Apple’s Photos app in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27’s biggest highlight is Siri AI, but the update also packs new features for apps like Messages, Notes, Wallet, and more. Here’s everything new for Apple’s Photos app in iOS 27.

New editing tools: Extend and Reframe, plus improved Clean Up

Apple Intelligence powers a trio of editing tools in iOS 27’s Photos app: Extend, Reframe, and a much-improved Clean Up feature.

Extend lets users “give their subjects more breathing room,” per Apple. For example, “they can straighten a crooked horizon without cropping out anything important, or adjust the aspect ratio, and Extend will fill in the missing pieces.”

Reframe lets you adjust the framing of your image spatially. Here’s how Apple describes it:

With Spatial Reframing, users can improve the composition of a photo after it’s been taken. Spatial Reframing builds on Apple’s deep understanding of spatial models thanks to Apple Vision Pro, so users can touch and drag a photo and preview in real time how the perspective shifts — as if they’d repositioned the camera in the original scene. Using powerful image models, Spatial Reframing will only generate new content where the perspective has been shifted, ensuring the reframed photo stays consistent with the original scene.

And the Clean Up feature that debuted in iOS 18 “gets a major upgrade,” Apple says, “so users can remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex.”

iCloud Shared Albums get their first major upgrades in years with iOS 27. The timing is likely no coincidence, with the feature perfect for Apple’s new HomeView product.

Here’s an overview of what’s new, per Apple:

Full resolution photos and videos

Shared Albums with Windows and Android

React with any emoji

Easier to save photos

Expire your Shared Albums

Additional participant permissions

New collections and organization tools

iOS 27 adds two new collections to the Photos app, available under Utilities.

Captured by Me exclusively contains photos taken by you. So it will filter out screenshots, photos you’ve saved from others, and so on.

Identity Documents scans through your Photos library and surfaces images that contain important reference documents, like your driver’s license or passport.

Apple says iOS 27 also adds “Album organization improvements,” but it doesn’t mention specifics.

Another new organization tool in iOS 27 is that you can add keywords to photos. Captions are still available too, but if you scroll up on a photo, near the bottom you’ll find a new ‘Add Keywords’ option.

Slideshow improvements

Another upgrade perfect for HomeView involves slideshow improvements.

Apple Photos has supported quick, easy slideshow creation for years. But if you wanted to customize the automatically generated slideshows, you were out of luck.

Now in iOS 27, slideshows offer new tools for customization. You can change the transition type, set a custom length for the full slideshow and for each photo, and more.

Another welcome addition is that Apple now lets you save any slideshow as a video with one tap.

Apple Photos in iOS 27: wrap-up

iOS 27 doesn’t contain any big changes to the design of the Photos app, so if you were hoping to go back to the pre-iOS 18 era, you’ll be disappointed. But the update does offer a variety of exciting new features that make iOS 27 a big release for Apple Photos.

title: Henry Cavill builds 16-bit ‘Mustache Protocol’ game on Googlebook for a good cause [Video]
snippet: As teased before the launch, Henry Cavill has built a video game on Googlebook, and it’s called Mustache Protocol. more…
fullText:
As teased before the launch, Henry Cavill has built a video game on Googlebook, and it’s called Mustache Protocol.

Fully embracing the Mission: Impossible – Fallout meme, this 16-bit video game is “about stopping rogue CGI artists from erasing every mustache on the planet.”

Part of the new platform’s promotional push heading into the holiday season, Google’s announcement says the actor:

“…used Rambler on his Googlebook to organize his thoughts as he brainstormed.”

“…mocked up different aesthetics, added accessories, and fine-tuned the design with Magic Pointer, which let him select and combine visual elements on screen.”

“…was able to move from his Android phone to his Googlebook and back without losing context or interrupting his creative flow” with Continue On

It looks like Cavill used Google Antigravity and other AI tools on the HP Googlebook 14 to “translate natural language prompts into working 16-bit game mechanics.”

	

The game is not yet available. When it launches, Google will “donate $11 for every play during the month of November” as part of a partnership with Movember. The company will donate up to $500,000 to “help support awareness and funding for men’s mental health, suicide prevention, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer.”

Until then, you can watch a three-part series that details how “Henry designed the hero character, vibe coded meme-inspired superpowers, and added to the game’s soundtrack.”

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 sales spike amid iPhone Duo release and ‘crackgate’ debacle
snippet: The iPhone Duo’s tumultuous debut seems to have some buyers looking to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 instead, as sales spiked in the week following Apple’s release. more…
fullText:
The iPhone Duo’s tumultuous debut seems to have some buyers looking to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 instead, as sales spiked in the week following Apple’s release.

The release of iPhone Duo was October 23 and, according to The Korea Herald, that same week is when sales of Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 spiked. 

Coincidence? Probably not.

The specifics here are that sales of Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 went up by 20% in Korea from October 23 through October 29. Exact numbers weren’t shared, but it does show a trend in Samsung’s foldable getting more attention in the wake of Apple’s first attempt at the form factor. In the days following Apple’s September announcement of the Duo, interest in Galaxy Z Fold 8 went up as well. 

	

There are any number of reasons why customers might be turning their attention to Samsung’s device. It could be the continued sales that make the Fold 8 a better deal overall, especially in Korea where the Fold 8 is considerably more affordable compared to the Duo. Other factors at play could include the messy implementation of unoptimized apps in Apple’s software, or even the iPhone Duo’s “crackgate” debacle that left a rough first impression, as a number of buyers were left with broken inner displays due to an apparent manufacturing error. There’s no evidence either way here yet, but there are plenty of potential reasons.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 is currently available for as low as $1,599, with Samsung rumored to be investing more heavily in the new form factor in 2027.

title: Instagram launches Edits for Mac with multi-track video editing and 4K exports
snippet: Instagram users can now download a Mac version of Edits, the company’s free video editing app, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, direct publishing to Instagram, and 4K exports. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Instagram users can now download a Mac version of Edits, the company’s free video editing app, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, direct publishing to Instagram, and 4K exports. Here are the details.

Instagram Edits comes to Mac

Instagram is launching Edits on desktop today, bringing its free video editing app to Mac with a larger workspace, more precise editing controls, and customizable keyboard shortcuts that can match those of other video editors.

Like Edits on mobile, Instagram says its desktop counterpart will receive weekly updates and is asking users for feedback to help shape future improvements.

Here’s Instagram:

A lot of creators have described the same moment to us: a project gets too big for your phone. You’ve got a dozen clips going, you’re trying to land a cut on the exact beat, and your thumb covers the part of the timeline you need to see. Your work is growing, and your tools should grow with it. We’re expanding Edits to take on your most ambitious projects on desktop.

One particularly interesting feature of the new desktop app is the ability to publish videos directly to Instagram, with support for native features such as tagging, location, and trial reels.

Instagram adds that it is expanding Edits to support “multiple aspect ratios (horizontal and vertical), with 4K watermark-free export, so you can easily share to any platform, or use Edits for personal projects.”

As for the actual editing tools, Edits for desktop makes basic operations like splitting, cutting, and trimming videos easier, while also offering a full multi-track timeline, keyframes for transitions, precise audio waveforms, and advanced color grading tools such as color wheels, curves, and log conversions.

Users can also import their own LUTs and fonts, customize keyboard shortcuts, and access Instagram’s licensed audio library.

Instagram says saved audio and text styles from the mobile app are already available on desktop. However, the ability to seamlessly edit the same project across Mac and mobile is still in development.

Instagram’s desktop Edits app also offers unlimited automatic captions with support for multiple languages, as well as hundreds of sound and video effects, all for free.

title: Reddit will soon be a ‘logged-in-only’ website, forcing you to have an account
snippet: Reddit is shifting to a “logged-in-only experience,” the company confirmed during its latest earnings call. more…
fullText:
Reddit is shifting to a “logged-in-only experience,” the company confirmed during its latest earnings call.

While the timeline is vague at this point, Reddit has confirmed that it will be locking down the site for users without an account, also impacting usage in private browsing modes. CEO Steve Huffman explains in a shareholder letter and a post on Reddit that the website will becoming a “logged-in-only experience.”

Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world.

In Q4 we’ll begin fully testing this in select markets outside the U.S. The results of those tests will inform an optimized version of logged-in-only Reddit globally.

The change also comes as Reddit says that search referral traffic was “down meaningfully” in Q3 2026, mainly in regards to logged-out traffic. “Down meaningfully” was later detailed to mean that traffic “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week.”

	

As for private browsing, Huffman says that Reddit has “rebuilt and [is] re-releasing incognito mode in our app.” 

	

Details on what will and will not be available to logged-out users are unclear at this time, though Huffman says that “the front page being available logged-out is useful and important,” adding that “visitors arriving from search or other external sources to see the content that’s being linked to.” He further implies that AI scraping is certainly a major part of this decision, saying that “the vast majority of unauthorized access to Reddit (basically the scraping and stealing of Reddit’s data) happens through our logged-out experiences.”

This comes shortly after Reddit rolled out a new personalized “For You” homepage.

title: Will Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pixel 12 mark the end of the flagship era of smartphones?
snippet: Like most Android fans, you probably enjoy having the latest and greatest smartphone buried in your pocket. The best camera, the best display, the fastest processor, and of course, as much RAM as any given smartphone OEM will pack in. And even as we’ve watched the typical flagship price balloon into the four-digit space, trade-in offers, carrier deals, and steep sales on certain hardware brands like Pixel have made it all too easy to keep up on what’s new in gadgets without breaking the bank year-in and year-out. more…
fullText:
Like most Android fans, you probably enjoy having the latest and greatest smartphone buried in your pocket. The best camera, the best display, the fastest processor, and of course, as much RAM as any given smartphone OEM will pack in. And even as we’ve watched the typical flagship price balloon into the four-digit space, trade-in offers, carrier deals, and steep sales on certain hardware brands like Pixel have made it all too easy to keep up on what’s new in gadgets without breaking the bank year-in and year-out.

Obviously, all of those routes towards a cheaper smartphone purchase still exist today — I assure you, anyone who regularly tunes into the NFL can recite Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T’s various deals by heart. But prices are rising so rapidly, with no sign of slowdown in sight, that I can no longer be sure any of those routes towards making new hardware more expensive will be available tomorrow. And honestly, we might hit a point where it’s increasingly difficult to recommend these phones to all but the most hardcore of enthusiasts, no matter how many sweeteners you add to the deal.

Throughout 2026, we’ve watched as new generations of barely-modified hardware have launched with $100 price hikes. We’ve watched as months-old hardware suddenly jumped up in price without so much in the way of a warning or an official announcement. And even outside of smartphones, you have to wonder if Google really hoped its latest lineup of laptops would’ve launched with more models available for under four figures. What’s been an underlying problem throughout the market throughout the last year, though, seems ready to burst into something much larger beginning throughout the next few months.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra already had a mid-cycle price hike, and its successor will likely cost even more.

Recent price leaks have not exactly filled me with confidence over what hardware to recommend to anyone in the market for a new phone. The Galaxy S27 Ultra is sounding like it could arrive starting at $1,500, $100 more than the S26 Ultra’s current MSRP and $200 more than what that phone launched at earlier this year. Motorola’s attempt to come back to the flagship space in the US for the first time since 2023 could be completely derailed by rumors of an even higher price point that guarantees it won’t appeal to anyone. And while we’re certainly too far out to really predict anything regarding Google’s next-gen Pixel pricing, if you think the Pixel 12 might be your next phone, I’d start saving today.

	

As you climb towards the $2,000 mark, it’s worth putting these costs into perspective. These are laptop prices — maybe not that new “PROLED” MacBook Pro, but certainly other upper-high end laptops from companies like Apple, Dell, and HP. $1,500 will buy you an mid-tier home treadmill, or a nice OLED TV, to say nothing of the truly practical ways you can put that much cash to good use in a time where the costs of everything is rising. While some might think there is no price ceiling that truly keeps them away from new Android hardware, I’d be willing to bet plenty of potential buyers are already being priced out of the high-end market entirely. We’re reaching a breaking point where the question might not even be about whether you can afford something, but whether you should, leaving customers with just two routes forward: keep your existing device, or opt for a midrange option when you can.

Sure, saying “no thanks” to something like the Pixel 11 Pro XL right now might be easy enough. But moving forward, practically every single Android user will need to set some kind of personal limit on the price of a new smartphone, and if you’re convinced the midrange space might serve as your sole savior, you might want to think again. While RAM prices are bound to affect the final cost of Google’s Pixel 12, those constraints on a final bill of materials might mean a whole lot more to something like the Pixel 11a. After all, when you’ve already seen the Pixel 10a and its generation-old Tensor G4 chipset get hit with a $100 price bump, you have to wonder if it’s time to cut back on certain “premium” features.

The Pixel 10a is already up to $600 at full price, and the Pixel 11a could cost even more.

The next few years of budget-oriented smartphones — and I really am talking about anything outside of the flagship space — is about to shift in a way we haven’t seen in over a decade. In the 2010s, cheap components and streamlined production costs helped bring about excellent midrange options like Google’s Pixel A-series, Samsung’s Galaxy A-series, and some select Moto G entries. Moving forward, these same companies will need to pick between higher prices and reduced spec sheets. The dream of yesterday’s flagship becoming tomorrow’s budget phone is, at least for the time being, dead and buried.

This isn’t just rampant speculation on my part. We’re already hearing about some companies making the decision to reduce RAM in their devices down to 8GB, 6GB, or even as low as 4GB, depending on the model and market it’s entering. It’s easy to see storage options also getting hit with their own downgrade — 128GB entry-level flagships could reemerge just as soon as they began to die off, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see 64GB options begin to reappear in sub-$600 models. That might be the sacrifice needed to keep other high-end features, like 120Hz OLED displays, hanging around in this price range.

	

Of course, you can’t simply opt to forego RAM or storage in the same way that you can downgrade the display, and with the memory crunch set to possibly extend to 2030 or beyond, there could come a time where cutting back on raw specs or non-essential features stops being an either-or question. The knock-on effect is obvious: If you suddenly have a lot more people buying devices with less horsepower than previous generations, you’re going to see a reciprocal slowdown of any software development that requires hardware capable of reaching a certain threshold. Widespread on-device AI, for those of you who care about local models, seems like a pipedream at this point, but these market conditions are just as likely to crush, say, any hope of more games with high-end graphics coming to Android.

It’s not that the hardware won’t exist to support these features — flagships will obviously still exist even if their price tags balloon over the $2,000 mark. It’s the audience size you have to worry about; for a large majority of developers, it simply won’t make sense to continue pushing the envelope for what constitutes a smaller and smaller crowd of potential users.

The other solution is to hold onto whatever device you have in your possession right now, for as long as you can. That might not sound particularly exciting — I know I couldn’t tell you the last time I went more than six months without changing phones, even discounting review units — but it’s also the most reasonable approach to the current crisis. It’s not too late to jump on a recent flagship (think 2024 or later) before things get particularly dire, either, and with holiday sales coming up, I’d urge anyone on the fence about upgrading their current device with the means to do so to pull the trigger. Tomorrow’s price, simply put, will not be today’s.

And hey, if there’s a silver lining to be found here, I think it’s this: we’ve seeing tech companies across the board — hardware and software alike — grow increasingly comfortable with the idea that, for the user, resources can be effectively unlimited. Those days are gone, and it’s going to force software developers, including Google, to make some changes that are probably long, long overdue. We might lose out on big hardware improvements, resource-heavy advancements, and flagship-esque affordable smartphones, but there’s always a chance Chrome’s memory usage finally gets under control. It might not be worth all of this pain, but it’s something, right?

title: ChatGPT and Work are merging soon, while ChatGPT Classic retires in January
snippet: Users who still rely on the ChatGPT Classic app were greeted today with a message informing them that the app will soon be retired. Separately, OpenAI is also preparing to merge ChatGPT and Work into a single interface. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Users who still rely on the ChatGPT Classic app were greeted today with a message informing them that the app will soon be retired. Separately, OpenAI is also preparing to merge ChatGPT and Work into a single interface. Here are the details.

ChatGPT Classic is going away

A few months ago, OpenAI released a new ChatGPT desktop app, which brought ChatGPT, Work, and Codex under a single interface. As a result, the regular ChatGPT app was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

The move proved controversial for two reasons. First, OpenAI replaced the native macOS app with an Electron-based version. Second, the new interface was extremely confusing, making it difficult to access regular ChatGPT conversations or even distinguish between ChatGPT, Work, and Codex.

OpenAI was quick to address some of the complaints, restoring direct access to conversations via a prominent Chat and Work toggle at the top of the window, along with a sidebar menu for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. The company has since introduced other changes to make the app easier to use.

The ChatGPT Classic app, on the other hand, remained largely untouched and became increasingly less reliable as OpenAI released new models that were more tightly integrated with features exclusive to the new app, such as the ability to select different reasoning effort levels.

And as much as it felt like the writing had been on the wall for its demise, now we have a date. According to a new message displayed to users when they open ChatGPT Classic, the app will officially be retired on January 30, 2027.

The banner reads:

“This app will retire on January 30, 2027. Get the latest features in the new ChatGPT app. Your full chat history comes with you, so you can pick up where you left off.”

Clicking on the banner leads users to the ChatGPT downloads page, where they can download the latest version of the desktop app.

OpenAI is merging ChatGPT and Work (and their allowances)

Meanwhile, OpenAI is informing users that it will begin testing a combined Chat and Work experience in the coming weeks.

The announcement comes a few months after OpenAI president Greg Brockman acknowledged that the new ChatGPT interface was “kind of a mess,” and said the company hoped to eliminate the Work tab by the end of the year, with its functionality becoming part of the regular ChatGPT experience.

Now, in an email sent to users, OpenAI explains that the test will start with a small group of users, who will be able to access ChatGPT’s conversational features and Work’s more advanced capabilities from the same interface:

This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app.

As part of the transition, OpenAI also plans to introduce a shared usage allowance for ChatGPT and Codex, replacing their separate limits.

According to the company, “most users won’t need to wait for their usage to reset more often than they do today.” OpenAI adds that “usage will depend on model and task, with more advanced models and complex tasks using more of your allowance. Unlimited Instant is included in your plan and will not draw from your usage.”
